explanation: Robert Burns sent it to a collection of Scottish songs in 1788, saying he had taken it down from an old man's singing. The song toasts friendships from long ago.

claims.text: The Scots phrase auld lang syne means roughly old long since, that is, days gone by.
Auld lang syne does not mean good health to all, a brand-new start or until we meet again.
In 1788 Robert Burns sent Auld Lang Syne to the Scots Musical Museum, a collection of Scottish songs.
Burns said he had taken the song down from an old man's singing.
Auld Lang Syne celebrates old friendships.
